summary: I reviewed .github/workflows/visual.yml, the cards.visual.spec.ts gate and the new test and baseline files. Container image tag: the version comes from package-lock.json and must match ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ before it is written to GITHUB_OUTPUT. That stops newline or output injection and keeps the image name on the official mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v<semver>-noble repo. A pull request can choose a different official tag, but that same pull request already runs its own code through npm ci, so nothing new is exposed. workflow_dispatch input 'update' is a boolean used only in if: expressions, never put into a run: script, so it can't be used for script injection. Only users with write access can dispatch the workflow. Permissions: the workflow sets contents: read at the top level and no job raises it. No secrets are referenced, and fork pull_request runs get a read-only token. Triggers: push and pull_request only, no pull_request_target or workflow_run, so untrusted code never runs with elevated rights. This matches ci.yml. Actions are pinned to full commit SHAs that match the pins already in ci.yml. The setup-node npm cache is scoped per ref by GitHub, so a pull request can't poison the cache on main. Artifacts: the uploads hold only *-linux.png baselines and playwright-report/, kept for 7 days. Neither path includes .git, where checkout stores its token, and no secrets reach the environment. Container --user 1001 runs without root. TLH_VISUAL_LINUX is a fixed value set in the workflow. Bringing the baselines in from run 44668550588 was a manual copy from this repo's own branch run, so it is trusted. No new dependencies. No BLOCKER, MAJOR, MINOR or NIT findings.
